title: Skillet Chicken Piccata with Lemon and Capers
description: Thin chicken cutlets seared until golden, then finished in a bright pan sauce of lemon, white wine, and briny capers. Good over pasta or rice, or with bread to catch the sauce.
notes: Storage: refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours in a covered container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a skillet over low heat with a splash of broth so the butter sauce does not separate. Substitutions: replace the wine with an equal amount of broth plus 1 extra tablespoon lemon juice. A gluten-free all-purpose blend or cornstarch works for the dredge. Capers and broth both carry salt, so taste the sauce before adding more. Food safety: cook chicken to 165°F in the thickest part.

ingredients.name: large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 1 1/2 lb total)
unsalted butter, cut into 4 pieces, divided

instructions: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 cutlets. Place them between two sheets of parchment and pound to an even 1/2-inch thickness. Pat dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Spread the flour in a shallow dish. Dredge each cutlet, pressing so the flour sticks, then shake off the excess.

Heat the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until the butter foams. Add the cutlets, working in two batches if they do not fit without touching, and cook until deep golden and 165°F in the thickest part, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits, then simmer until reduced by about half, about 2 minutes.
Add the broth, lemon juice, and capers. Simmer briskly until the sauce has reduced by about a third and lightly coats a spoon, 4 to 5 minutes.

Turn the heat to low and whisk in the remaining 3 tablespoons butter one piece at a time until the sauce is glossy. Return the chicken and any juices to the pan along with the lemon slices, turn to coat, and warm through for 1 minute. Scatter with parsley and serve.

title: Citrus-Marinated Carne Asada Tacos
description: Skirt steak soaked in orange, lime, garlic, and cumin, seared hard in a hot pan and chopped for warm corn tortillas. Onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime are all it needs.
notes: Marinating: plan on 2 to 8 hours in the refrigerator. Longer than 8 hours and the citrus starts to make the surface of the meat mushy. Discard the used marinade; do not serve it. Doneness: 130 to 135°F gives medium-rare; the USDA recommends 145°F with a 3-minute rest for whole cuts of beef. Flank steak is thicker than skirt and needs 4 to 5 minutes per side. On a grill, cook over high direct heat with the same timing. Use tortillas made from 100% corn (check the label) to keep the dish gluten-free. Storage: refrigerate leftover steak within 2 hours for up to 3 days and reheat quickly in a hot skillet.

ingredients.name: neutral oil such as avocado or canola, divided
skirt steak or flank steak, cut into pieces that fit the pan

instructions: In a shallow dish or zip-top bag, combine the orange juice, lime juice, 2 tablespoons of the oil, the garlic, jalapeño, 1/2 cup of the cilantro, the cumin, chili powder, 1 1/2 teaspoons of the salt, and the pepper. Add the steak and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours and up to 8 hours.
Take the steak out of the refrigerator 20 minutes before cooking. Lift it from the marinade, discard the marinade, and pat the steak very dry with paper towels so it sears instead of steaming.

Heat a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over high heat until it just begins to smoke, 3 to 4 minutes, and turn on the vent fan. Add half of the remaining tablespoon of oil, then lay in half of the steak. Sear without moving until deeply browned, 2 to 3 minutes per side for skirt steak, to 130 to 135°F for medium-rare or 145°F for medium. Repeat with the remaining oil and steak.
Transfer the steak to a cutting board, tent loosely with foil, and rest for 10 minutes.

While the steak rests, wipe out the skillet and set it over medium-high heat. Warm the tortillas a few at a time until pliable and lightly charred in spots, 20 to 30 seconds per side. Stack them in a clean towel to keep warm.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain, then chop it into bite-size pieces. Toss with the juices on the board and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Fill the tortillas with steak and top with the diced onion, the remaining 1/4 cup cilantro, and avocado if using. Serve with lime wedges.

title: Beef Bulgogi Rice Bowls
description: Thinly sliced beef marinated with soy, pear, garlic, and sesame, then seared in a very hot skillet until the edges caramelize. Served over rice with scallions and cool cucumber.
notes: Slicing: 30 to 45 minutes in the freezer firms the beef enough to cut very thin; many markets also sell pre-sliced beef for bulgogi. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours, and discard any marinade left in the bowl. Substitutions: a sweet apple such as Fuji stands in for Asian pear. Gluten-free tamari replaces the soy sauce if you need to avoid wheat. For heat, stir 1 tablespoon gochujang into the marinade (check the label; many brands contain wheat). Storage: refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 3 days. The raw marinated beef freezes well for up to 2 months; thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

ingredients.name: boneless ribeye or top sirloin, sliced 1/8 inch thick against the grain
Asian pear, peeled and grated (about 1/3 cup)
fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated
scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
neutral oil such as canola, divided

instructions: If slicing the beef yourself, freeze it for 30 to 45 minutes until firm at the edges, then cut it across the grain into slices about 1/8 inch thick.

In a large bowl, stir together the grated pear, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, pepper, and scallion whites until the sugar dissolves. Add the beef and sliced onion and toss with your hands until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours.

Heat a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over high heat until very hot, 2 to 3 minutes. Add 1 teaspoon of the oil. Lift about a third of the beef and onion from the marinade, letting the excess drip back into the bowl, and spread it in a single layer.

Cook without stirring until the underside is browned at the edges, 1 to 2 minutes, then flip and stir until the beef is cooked through and the juices have reduced to a glaze, about 1 minute more. Transfer to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining oil and beef in two more batches, letting the pan reheat for 30 seconds between batches. Discard the marinade left in the bowl.
Return all of the beef to the skillet and toss over high heat for 30 seconds to rewarm. Spoon over the rice and top with the scallion greens, sesame seeds, and cucumber slices if using.

title: Chicken Souvlaki Skewers with Tzatziki
description: Chicken thighs marinated in lemon, garlic, and oregano, cooked on skewers until charred at the edges, and served in warm pita with a cool cucumber-yogurt sauce.
notes: Marinating: at least 1 hour and up to 8 hours in the refrigerator; discard the used marinade. On an outdoor grill, cook over medium-high direct heat with the same timing. Make-ahead: the tzatziki keeps covered in the refrigerator for 3 days and tastes better after an hour. Substitutions: chicken breast works but dries out faster, so pull it right at 165°F. Serve over rice or salad instead of pita for a gluten-free plate. Storage: refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 3 days. Food safety: cook chicken to 165°F.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/4-inch pieces

instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk 3 tablespoons of the olive oil with the lemon juice, vinegar, minced garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper. Add the chicken and toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour and up to 8 hours.

For the tzatziki, wrap the grated cucumber in a clean towel and squeeze out as much liquid as you can. Stir it into the yogurt with the grated garlic, lemon juice, dill, and salt. Cover and refrigerate until serving.
Thread the chicken onto 8 skewers, leaving a little space between pieces so the heat can reach all sides. Discard the marinade left in the bowl.

Heat a grill pan or 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes, then brush it with half of the remaining tablespoon of oil. Add 4 skewers and cook, turning every 2 to 3 minutes, until charred in spots and 165°F in the center of the largest piece, 10 to 12 minutes.
Transfer the skewers to a plate and rest for 5 minutes. Brush the pan with the remaining oil and cook the second batch the same way.
Warm the pitas in the hot pan until soft and lightly toasted, about 30 seconds per side. Serve the skewers with the pita, tzatziki, and sliced red onion.

title: Classic Double Smash Burgers
description: Two thin, crisp-edged beef patties with melted American cheese, pickles, and a tangy burger sauce on a butter-toasted bun. The hard smash in a very hot skillet is what builds the crust.
notes: Use 80% lean beef; leaner beef will not form the same crust and dries out. No oil is needed in the pan since the beef renders its own fat. Expect smoke, so run the vent fan. Make-ahead: the sauce keeps for 5 days refrigerated, and the beef can be portioned into balls a day ahead and kept cold. Substitutions: sharp cheddar melts less smoothly but works. Buns and mayonnaise vary by brand, so check labels for sesame and soy if those matter to you. Food safety: ground beef should reach 160°F; patties this thin get there by the time the cheese melts and no pink remains. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
instructions: Stir together the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, and chopped pickle in a small bowl. Refrigerate until needed.
Divide the beef into 8 equal portions of about 3 ounces each and roll them loosely into balls without packing. Keep them in the refrigerator while you toast the buns.
Heat a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Spread the butter on the cut sides of the buns and toast them cut-side down, two at a time, until golden, 1 to 2 minutes. Set aside.

Raise the heat to high and heat the dry skillet until it just begins to smoke, 2 to 3 minutes. Place 2 or 3 beef balls well apart in the pan. Lay a small square of parchment on each and press down hard with a sturdy spatula until the patty is about 1/4 inch thick, holding for 10 seconds. Peel off the parchment and season the tops with some of the salt and pepper.

Cook without moving until the edges are deep brown and lacy and juices bubble up through the top, 1 1/2 to 2 minutes. Scrape firmly under each patty to keep the crust attached, flip, and top each with a slice of cheese. Cook until the cheese melts and no pink remains, 45 to 60 seconds, to 160°F.
Stack the patties in pairs on a plate. Scrape the pan clean, let it reheat for 30 seconds, and repeat with the remaining beef, salt, pepper, and cheese.
Spread sauce on both halves of each bun. Layer the bottom buns with pickle chips, a double patty, sliced onion, and lettuce if using, then close and serve right away.

title: Weeknight Butter Chicken
description: Yogurt-marinated chicken thighs simmered in a smooth tomato sauce with garam masala, ginger, butter, and cream. Mild, rich, and made for spooning over basmati rice.
notes: Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours. Gluten-free: the ingredients are naturally gluten-free, but check that your garam masala and chili powder are single-spice or labeled gluten-free, and serve with rice rather than naan. Heat level is mild; add up to 1/4 teaspoon more cayenne for a warmer curry. Substitutions: chicken breast works if you cut the final simmer to 5 to 6 minutes; full-fat coconut milk can replace the cream, though the dish still contains milk from the butter and yogurt. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. The flavor deepens overnight. Food safety: cook chicken to 165°F.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated
Kashmiri chili powder (or 1 tsp sweet paprika plus 1/8 tsp cayenne)

instructions: In a mixing bowl, stir the chicken with the yogurt, lemon juice, 2 teaspoons of the garam masala, the turmeric, and 1 teaspoon of the salt. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours.

Heat the oil in a Dutch oven or deep 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Shake excess marinade off half of the chicken and add it in a single layer. Cook until browned in spots, 2 to 3 minutes per side; it will not be cooked through. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the rest of the chicken.

Reduce the heat to medium and melt 2 tablespoons of the butter. Add the onion and cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, until soft and golden, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add the remaining 1 teaspoon garam masala and the chili powder and stir for 30 seconds. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and water, then add the sugar and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Partially cover and simmer over medium-low heat until slightly thickened and a shade darker, about 10 minutes. For a smooth sauce, blend it in the pot with an immersion blender.
Return the chicken and its juices to the pot. Simmer uncovered, stirring now and then, until the chicken is tender and 165°F in the center, 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream and the remaining 1 tablespoon butter and simmer for 2 minutes until the sauce is glossy and coats a spoon. Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed. Serve over basmati rice.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
description: Tender slices of flank steak and crisp-tender broccoli in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce. Faster than takeout once the slicing is done.
notes: Have everything sliced and the sauce mixed before you turn on the heat; the cooking goes quickly. Slicing the steak is easier after 20 minutes in the freezer. Allergens: oyster sauce is made from oysters and usually contains wheat and soy. A vegetarian mushroom stir-fry sauce can replace it for a shellfish-free version, and gluten-free tamari plus gluten-free oyster sauce make the dish gluten-free. Substitutions: sirloin or skirt steak for flank; broccolini or green beans for broccoli. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 3 days and reheat in a skillet with a splash of water to loosen the sauce.

ingredients.name: flank steak, sliced 1/4 inch thick against the grain
neutral oil such as canola, divided
broccoli crowns, cut into bite-size florets (about 6 cups)

instructions: Toss the sliced steak with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 2 teaspoons cornstarch in a bowl until evenly coated. Let it stand for 15 minutes while you prepare everything else.
In a small bowl, whisk the broth, 3 tablespoons soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, 1 tablespoon cornstarch, sesame oil, and pepper until smooth.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a 12-inch skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the broccoli and stir for 1 minute, then add the water, cover, and steam until bright green and crisp-tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate and wipe the pan dry.

Return the pan to high heat and add 1 tablespoon of the oil. When it just begins to smoke, spread half of the beef in a single layer. Cook without stirring until browned underneath, about 1 minute, then flip and cook until no longer pink, 30 to 60 seconds more. Transfer to the plate with the broccoli. Repeat with the remaining oil and beef.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic and ginger to the oil left in the pan and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Whisk the sauce again, pour it in, and simmer, stirring constantly, until thick and glossy, 1 to 2 minutes.
Return the beef, broccoli, and any juices to the pan and toss until everything is coated and heated through, about 1 minute. Serve over steamed rice.

title: Oven-Roasted Jerk-Style Chicken Thighs
description: Bone-in chicken thighs marinated in a paste of scallions, Scotch bonnet, allspice, thyme, and lime, then roasted hot until the skin is dark and crisp. Spicy, fragrant, and good with rice and beans or a crunchy slaw.
equipment: rimmed sheet pan with wire rack
notes: Marinating: at least 4 hours and up to 24 hours in the refrigerator; discard any marinade left behind. Heat: one seeded Scotch bonnet gives a firm but manageable burn. Leave the seeds in or use two chiles for more, or swap in a jalapeño for a mild version. Wear gloves when handling the chile and the marinade, and avoid touching your eyes. Substitutions: gluten-free tamari replaces the soy sauce; 1 teaspoon dried thyme replaces fresh. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days; reheat at 375°F for 12 to 15 minutes to re-crisp the skin. Food safety: chicken is safe at 165°F, and thighs are most tender between 175 and 185°F.

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet or habanero chile, stemmed and seeded
fresh ginger, peeled and roughly chopped

instructions: Combine the scallions, chile, garlic, ginger, lime juice, soy sauce, oil, brown sugar, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a blender or food processor. Blend to a coarse paste, 30 to 45 seconds, scraping down the sides once.

Pat the chicken dry and cut two shallow slashes through the skin side of each thigh. Wearing gloves, rub the marinade all over the chicken and under the skin in a large bowl or zip-top bag. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours and up to 24 hours.

Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper-middle position. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil and set a wire rack on top. Arrange the thighs skin-side up on the rack with space between them, leaving a coating of marinade on each piece. Discard the rest of the marinade.
Roast until the skin is deep brown and charred at the edges and the thickest part of a thigh, away from the bone, reads at least 165°F and ideally 175°F, 35 to 40 minutes.
For more char, switch the oven to broil on high and broil for 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely so the sugar in the marinade does not burn.
Rest the chicken for 5 to 10 minutes, then serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

title: Cider-Braised Pork Shoulder with Apples and Onions
description: Pork shoulder browned and slowly braised in apple cider, mustard, and thyme until it pulls apart with a fork, with soft onions and apple wedges in a reduced pan sauce. Mostly hands-off oven time.
notes: Use fresh, unfiltered apple cider or unsweetened apple juice, not cider vinegar; dry hard cider also works. Choose apples that hold their shape, such as Honeycrisp, Pink Lady, or Granny Smith. Doneness: whole cuts of pork are safe at 145°F with a 3-minute rest, but shoulder only turns tender once it reaches roughly 195 to 205°F, so cook by feel until a fork twists easily in the meat. Make-ahead: the braise is better the next day. Chill it in its liquid, lift off the solidified fat, and reheat covered at 300°F for about 30 minutes. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. The recipe contains mustard. If cooking gluten-free, check the labels on the broth and mustard.

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder, trimmed of thick surface fat and cut into 4 large pieces
medium yellow onions, sliced 1/4 inch thick
firm apples, cored and cut into 8 wedges each

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the lower third. Pat the pork dry and season it all over with the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Brown the pork in two batches, turning with tongs, until deep brown on all sides, 6 to 7 minutes per batch. Transfer to a plate.

Pour off all but about 2 tablespoons of fat and reduce the heat to medium. Add the onions and cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, until soft and golden, 7 to 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook until the paste darkens, about 1 minute.

Pour in the cider and scrape the bottom of the pot clean. Stir in the broth, vinegar, and mustard, add the thyme and bay leaves, and bring to a simmer. Return the pork and its juices to the pot; the liquid should come about halfway up the meat.
Cover and transfer to the oven. Braise for 2 hours, turning the pork over once halfway through.
Tuck the apple wedges around the pork, cover again, and braise until a fork twists easily in the meat and the apples are tender but still holding their shape, 30 to 45 minutes more.

Move the pork and apples to a platter with a slotted spoon and tongs. Discard the thyme stems and bay leaves and skim the fat from the surface of the liquid. Simmer the sauce over medium-high heat until reduced by about a third and lightly syrupy, 8 to 10 minutes. Taste and add up to 1/2 teaspoon more salt if needed.
Pull the pork into large chunks and spoon the sauce and onions over the top. Serve with the apples alongside.

title: Spiced Turkey Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
description: Tender turkey meatballs seasoned with cumin, garlic, and cilantro, simmered in a paprika-warmed tomato sauce. Made without gluten or dairy, and good over rice or potatoes.
notes: Gluten-free: oats are often processed alongside wheat, so buy oats labeled certified gluten-free, and check that your spices are single-ingredient or labeled gluten-free. Substitutions: ground chicken works in place of turkey; flat-leaf parsley can replace cilantro. Avoid 99% lean turkey, which cooks up dry. Make-ahead: shape the meatballs up to a day ahead and keep them covered in the refrigerator. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days, or freeze the cooked meatballs in their sauce for up to 3 months. Reheat gently, covered, with a splash of water. Food safety: ground turkey must reach 165°F in the center.
instructions: In a large bowl, stir together the oats, egg, 2 cloves' worth of the minced garlic, 2 tablespoons of the cilantro, 1 teaspoon of the cumin, 1 teaspoon of the salt, and the pepper. Let stand for 5 minutes so the oats soften.
Add the turkey and mix gently with a fork or your hands until just combined; overmixing makes the meatballs tough. With damp hands, shape the mixture into 20 meatballs about 1 1/2 inches across.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a deep 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the meatballs, in two batches if the pan is crowded, and brown on two or three sides, 4 to 5 minutes total per batch. They will not be cooked through. Transfer to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and the onion. Cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, until soft and translucent, 5 to 6 minutes. Add the remaining garlic, the paprika, the remaining 1 teaspoon cumin, and the cayenne, and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, water, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and bring to a simmer.

Nestle the meatballs and any juices into the sauce. Cover, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer gently, turning the meatballs once, until they reach 165°F in the center and the sauce has thickened slightly, 12 to 15 minutes.
Taste the sauce and add a pinch more salt if needed. Sprinkle with the remaining 2 tablespoons cilantro and serve.
